Rinkos konsultacijos tikslas 2.1. Šios rinkos konsultacijos tikslas – išanalizuoti rinkos galimybes, įvertinti, ar parengtas techninės specifikacijos projektas nepagrįstai neriboja tiekėjų konkurencijos, patikslinti techninius reikalavimus, sužinoti realius transporto priemonių pristatymo terminus bei orientacinę pirkimo rinkos kainą. 3. Konsultacijos eiga ir terminai 3.1. Pastabos, pasiūlymai ir užpildytas klausimynas teikiami tik Centrinės viešųjų pirkimų informacinės sistemos (CVP IS) susirašinėjimo priemonėmis iki 2026 m. lapkričio 27 d. 12:00 val. 4. Konfidencialumas ir teisinės pasekmės 4.1. Rinkos konsultacijos metu gauta informacija bus naudojama tik Pirkimo dokumentų rengimui. Perkančioji organizacija užtikrina, kad konsultacijos metu gauti duomenys nebus panaudoti siekiant iškreipti konkurenciją ar pažeisti nediskriminavimo ir skaidrumo principus. 4.2. title: Madservice - Nordfyns Kommune
description: Nordfyns Kommune ønsker at udbyde madservice inkl. udbringning/levering til hjemmeboende borgere. Udbuddet omfatter ikke levering af mad til borgere, der bor på Kommunens plejecentre. Madservice er en ydelse tildelt efter § 13 i Ældreloven (LBK nr .1651 af 30/12/2024) og/eller Servicelovens §83 (LBK nr 1287 af 28/08/2020). Borgere i eget hjem tildeles ydelsen i henhold til Ældrelovens bestemmelser i § 18 om frit valg samt. Servicelovens § 91. Loven har til formål at sikre, at borgere i eget hjem, der er visiteret til madservice, har frit leverandørvalg. Opgaven omfatter madservice med udbringning, dvs. produktion og levering af mad. Nordfyns Kommune har estimeret det samlede opgaveomfang til at udgøre: • Gennemsnitlig 1.200 portioner pr. uge (hovedretter). Hertil kommer tilkøb af biretter og madpakker. Omfanget er opgjort på baggrund af perioden juni 2025 – maj 2026 (begge inkl). Da borgerne har frit valg mellem leverandører, er omfanget af ydelser efter Aftalen, dels afhængigt af, hvor mange borgere der er berettiget til en visitation til madservice, og dels af borgernes konkrete valg af leverandør. Nordfyns Kommune således ikke sikre leverandøren et minimums køb i aftaleperioden.

title: Netherlands – Property management services of real estate on a fee or contract basis – Leegstandbeheer
description: De gemeente beschikt over een omvangrijke vastgoedportefeuille, waaronder gebouwen en percelen grond (hierna te noemen onroerend goed), die wordt ingezet ter realisatie van maatschappelijke doelstellingen op onder andere het gebied van cultuur, welzijn, sport en onderwijs: maatschappelijke doelstellingen. De Vastgoedorganisatie Utrecht (hierna: VGU) vervult namens de gemeente de eigenaarsrol ten aanzien van dit onroerend goed. Als gevolg van onder meer mutaties, herontwikkeling, verkoop of gewijzigde beleidsinzet kan gemeentelijk onroerend goed tijdelijk leeg komen te staan. Daarom vindt de gemeente het belangrijk dat het onroerend goed veilig wordt beheerd, waarbij ook rekening wordt gehouden met het minimaliseren van de beheerskosten. Ook vindt de gemeente het belangrijk dat het onroerend goed maatschappelijk wordt benut, tenzij dat niet mogelijk is. €400.000,- over 4 jaar.

title: France – Construction work for multi-dwelling buildings and individual houses – BEFA GRAVELINES 1
description: Il s'agit du premier appel d'offre d’une série de cinq visant la prise à bail en l'état futur d’achèvement (BEFA) en loyer libre de logements neufs situés dans un périmètre de 30 minutes de la centrale de Gravelines. Cette première opération porte sur la réalisation et la mise à disposition de 75 logements (5 T2,35 T3,35 T4) en plusieurs programmes destinés à être livrés à l’horizon 2030. La prise à bail par EDF pourra représenter jusqu’à 50 % d’un programme immobilier limitée à 20 logements individuels ou collectifs. Cette part pourra toutefois atteindre 100 % pour des opérations de taille réduite comprise entre 5 et 9 logements. L'objectif présenté constitue une cible minimale. En cas d'opportunités complémentaires, le donneur d'ordre se réserve la possibilité d'augmenter le volume de logements jusqu'à 20 % supplémentaire et se réserve la possibilité de substituer des lots d’une typologie à l’autre.

title: Austria – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – DION 136 – KI-Telefonvermittlung
description: Die Burgenländische Krankenanstalten-Gesellschaft m.b.H. Die Lösung nimmt eingehende Anrufe automatisiert entgegen, erkennt das Anliegen in natürlicher Sprache, erteilt Standardauskünfte, vermittelt an die zuständige Stelle, nimmt Nachrichten und Rückrufwünsche strukturiert auf und stellt jederzeit die Übergabe an einen Menschen sicher; in einer Ausbaustufe unterstützt sie die Terminvergabe. title: User Testing Software Platform for User Experience Testing
description: Notice of Proposed Procurement (NPP) for User Testing Software Platform for User Experience Testing This bid solicitation 1000505276/B cancels and supersedes previous bid solicitation number 1000505276/A dated November 03, 2025 with a closing of December 03, 2025 at 02:00 PM EDT. The solicitation is being reissued as the previous solicitations resulted in non compliant bids. Unless otherwise stated herein, all terms and conditions of the original solicitation remain unchanged. The Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) intends to enter into a contract with a single contractor for access to a user testing software platform to test CRA content on Canada.ca with the Canadian public, as well as certain niche audiences such as business owners, families with children, and other demographics as required. The ability to test with persons who use assistive reading and navigation technologies is not within scope for this requirement and has been solicited under a separate procurement by the CRA. The objective is to assess the ease with which users can find information and successfully complete tasks on Canada.ca and to identify any difficulties that users face in navigating CRA content so that solutions can be proposed and implemented to improve those performance measures. This requirement also includes irrevocable options to procure additional quantities of test requests to be used within the User Testing Software Platform annual entity license for the User Testing Software Platform for User Experience Testing. The period of any resulting contract will be for two (2) years with CRA retaining the irrevocable option to extend the period of the contract for up to five (5) additional one (1) year periods. A bid must comply with the requirements of the bid solicitation and meet all mandatory evaluation criteria to be declared responsive. The responsive bid with the lowest bid evaluation price will be recommended for contract award. Proposal documents and supporting information must be submitted in either English or French. Conditional Set-Aside Under the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business • This procurement may be conditionally set aside under the federal government Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business. • In order to be considered for the set-aside, the Bidder must certify that it qualifies as an Indigenous business as defined under PSIB and that it will comply with all requirements of PSIB. If bids from two (2) or more Indigenous businesses are compliant with the terms of the Request for Proposal, the contracting authority will limit the competition to those Indigenous businesses and will not consider bids from any non-Indigenous businesses that may have been submitted. • For more information on Indigenous business requirements of the Set-aside Program for Indigenous Business, refer to Eligibility for Indigenous procurement set aside and Procurement information for Indigenous business owners Questions must be directed in writing to the contracting authority via email: Christian.Nkezurukundo@cra-arc.gc.ca Bids must be submitted by using the Connect service provided by the Canada Post Corporation. When responding, the proposal MUST be delivered to: Canada Revenue Agency Bid Receiving Unit BRUg@cra-arc.gc.ca Bids will not be accepted if emailed directly to this email address. This email address must be used to request that CRA open a Connect conversation, as detailed in Appendix 3: Standard Instructions - Goods or Services - Competitive Requirements of the Request for Proposal. Bidders must not use their own licensing agreement for Connect to initiate a Connect conversation with CRA. The CRA reserves the right to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement.

title: Biohazardous Waste Removal Services
description: Title: Biohazardous Waste Removal Services The Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) has a requirement of biohazardous waste removal services for the Ottawa Laboratory Fallowfield (OLF), in accordance with the Statement of Work at Annex Statement of Work. The initial contract shall be for a period of three (3) years, with four (4) one-year option periods at the sole discretion of the Agency. For additional information, consult the section on Security Clearances in the Offeror Requirements, and the section on security in the resulting contract. This means that only Canadian Suppliers and Suppliers of an Applicable Trading Partner, as defined in the Annex Solicitation of Offers Definitions, are eligible for this solicitation of offers. Offers submitted by Suppliers of a Non-Trading Partner will be rejected. Set-aside for Indigenous Business Canada has set aside this procurement under the federal government Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business. This set aside is a measure with respect to Indigenous peoples under Article 800 of the Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA) and a measure with respect to Aboriginal peoples or a set-asides for small and minority business under the international trade agreements. CONDITIONAL SET-ASIDE: This procurement has been conditionally set aside under the federal government's Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). The procurement is open to both Indigenous and non-Indigenous businesses. However, if two or more Indigenous businesses submit a bid, then the procurement is set aside under PSIB. In order to be considered under PSIB, a supplier must certify that it qualifies as an Indigenous business as defined under PSIB and that it will comply with all requirements of PSIB. Inquiries regarding this requirement must be submitted to the Contracting Authority: Ashley Bennett Senior Procurement and Contracting Officer Contracting and Procurement Policy Division Canadian Food Inspection Agency 1400 Merivale Road, Ottawa, ON K1A 0Y9 Ashley.Bennett@inspection.gc.ca The Bid Receiving Email Address is Solely for Delivery of Bids. No other communications are to be forwarded to this email address.

title: Counter Uncrewed Aerial Systems (C-UAS) technology with optional risk mitigation capability
description: This requirement is for: The Correctional Service of Canada, all regions (Pacific, Prairies, Ontario, Quebec, and Atlantic). Trade agreement: Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA), World Trade Organisation-Agreement on Government Procurement (WTO-AGP), Canada Ukraine Free-Trade Agreement (CUFTA), Canada Korea Trade Agreement (CKTA), Canada free trade agreements with Chile/Colombia/Honduras/Panama, Canada-Peru Free Trade Agreement, Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) and Canada-United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement (Canada-UK TCA), Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP). Policy on Reciprocal Procurement: This solicitation is open only to Canadian suppliers and to Suppliers of an applicable trading partner. Competitive Procurement Strategy: Pass or Fail. This is an invitation to qualify (ITQ). Suppliers must achieve a rating of Pass on all Mandatory Criteria in order to qualify. Nature of Requirements: The following is a summary of the ITQ for this requirement: The Correctional Service of Canada (CSC) is seeking to qualify suppliers capable of leasing Counter Uncrewed Aerial Systems (C-UAS) technology and related optional risk mitigation capabilities for use at federal correctional institutions across Canada. Qualification does not constitute technical compliance with any subsequent requirement. Suppliers must comply with the evaluation process contained in any subsequent solicitation documents in order to be considered compliant. Objectives: The objective of this ITQ is to establish a list of qualified suppliers that have demonstrated experience and capability in providing C-UAS technologies and services. title: Mapping Canada's Advanced Manufacturing Capabilities
description: The Department of Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED) is seeking professional services to conduct a comprehensive assessment and mapping of Canada's advanced manufacturing ecosystem. The work involves identifying and analyzing Canadian capabilities, assets, firms, research institutions, industry associations, government programs, and test facilities across five technology domains: robotics and automation, additive manufacturing, smart factories and digitally enabled production systems, advanced materials and composites manufacturing, and advanced tooling and precision manufacturing. The Contractor will assess Canada's strengths, weaknesses, gaps, sovereign capabilities, and national security considerations; benchmark Canadian capabilities against leading international jurisdictions; estimate market opportunities and investment requirements; and provide strategic recommendations to support future policy development, investment prioritization, workforce development, and ecosystem coordination. title: Weak magnetic anomaly detection for defence and security
description: ***AMENDMENT 001 - An attachment has been added. The document contains questions and answers related to the Challenge.*** *Please note that the ISC website will be available on October 30, 2026* This Challenge Notice is issued under the Innovative Solutions Canada Program (ISC) Call for Proposals 004 (EN578-24ISC4). For general ISC information, Offerors can visit the ISC website at: https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/innovative-solutions-canada/en Please refer to the Solicitation Documents Innovative Solutions Canada Program Call for Proposals – 004 - Tender Notice | CanadaBuys https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities/tender-notice/cb-331-17030872 which contains the process for submitting a proposal. Steps to apply: Step 1: Read this challenge. Step 2: Read the Call for Proposals : https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities/tender-notice/cb-331-17030872 Step 3: Propose your solution here : https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/innovative-solutions-canada/en/weak-magnetic-anomaly-detection-defence-and-security?auHash=1sFpxB6DzXI5S5IfIex1eysacfiS2cUIMVE1Eeit0EQ ISED is seeking a novel magnetometer (either quantum or classical or a combination thereof) that provides advantage over existing capabilities either in sensitivity, specificity, or Size, Weight, Power and Cost (SWaP-C), and multi-domain employability. Challenge sponsor: Innovation, Sciences et Développement économique Canada (ISDE) Funding mechanism: Contract Opening date: October 30, 2026 Closing date: November 27, 2026 14:00 Eastern time Challenge Problem statement Canada has a requirement for magnetic anomaly detection for defence and security. Traditional magnetometers, such as fluxgate sensors, have been used for decades to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. A fluxgate magnetometer is a relatively simple classical device: it consists of a coil of wire wrapped around a core material and detects changes in magnetic flux passing through the sensor. While reliable, these classical sensors face inherent limitations in size, sensitivity, accuracy, and long term stability. Quantum magnetometers, by contrast, leverage the principles of quantum mechanics and promise the ability to achieve superior performance. They offer enhanced sensitivity, improved accuracy and stability, and in some cases even reduced size and weight compared to their classical counterparts. There is a lack of suitably mature quantum sensors in the commercial space. The government of Canada has identified a need to develop a device or system consisting of hardware and software and a quantum sensor or a mix of classical and quantum sensors capable of sensing nanotesla (nT) or even femtotesla (fT) magnetic signals that can be used for a myriad of commercial, medical, and defence applications. In scanning the research underway, there appears to be interest in various means for the sensing of magnetic fields, including but not limited to Superconducting Quantum Interference Devices (SQUID), Superconducting Quantum Interference Filter (SQIF), and (Nitrogen Vacancy (NV) diamond. In addition to this we are led to believe that Rydberg atoms, typically framed for electric field detection can be reconfigured and/or adapted for magnetic field detection as well. We are also aware of another technology termed Spin-Exchange Relaxation-Free (SERF) which is very sensitive, but so sensitive as to be problematic to employ. This investigation seeks to explore nT and even fT sensitivities. Desired outcomes and considerations Essential (mandatory) outcomes The proposed solution must: 1. Essential range and direction finding considerations Demonstrate sensing capabilities of magnetic anomalies in close proximity where distance (d) is greater than or equal to (=) 2 meters (m) with a relative error less than 10%. The device must provide azimuth to +/- 5 degrees, and an inclination of +/- 5 degrees. 2. Sensitivity Produce a prototype capable of a minimum of 500 picotesla (pT) sensitivity with a target of 10 fT. 3. Specificity The device must be able to separate a target signal from background noise. A sensitive magnetometer will detect a plethora of magnetic fields in a given cluttered environment, but the user will be interested in the absence or presence of a target signal. The device must detect and identify three specific Steel 1018 ferromagnetic targets at a minimum distance of 10 meter through free space. It must achieve a 95% true positive rate (TPR) for both detecting the presence of a target and classifying which specific target is present. 4. Rough characterization Demonstrate ability to characterize the nature of the source in rough order of magnitude – i.e. point source vs larger objects +/- 5 centimeters (cm). 5. Latency Readout less than or equal to (=) 200 milliseconds (ms) meaning sensing, ranging, azimuth, and inclination reading allowing dynamic device sensor use for object or enclosure survey. This 200 ms is the total time from sensing to displaying the result to the human user. This time includes physical sensing, processing to the point the user is provided useful data. 6. Sense through barrier capability Ability for device to sense through paramagnetic barrier materials such as walls (including but not limited to wood, gypsum board, plaster, insulation material) with some barriers inundated with clutter from other materials such as steel studs, nails, screws, pipes and other ferromagnetic materials. 7. Prototype description All parts/components fully integrated in one system of systems, including but not limited to power, API/software, hardware (sensor, cooler – if applicable). 8. Power Power consumption must be 50 W or less. Integrated replaceable power supply offering at least eight (8) hours of cordless and continued operation at temperatures ranging between 16°C and 40°C at a relative humidity between 30 and 60%. 9. Human factors Must be lightweight and compact/portable (e.g.; hand-carried, “shoulderable”, body worn). 10. Size and weight Volumetric dimensions =117,232 cm^3 (77 x 52.5 x 29 cm); maximum weight = 15Kg. 11. Environmental considerations The initial device must be designed at least for indoor use at temperatures ranging between 16°C to 30°C with relative humidity between 30-60% 12. Per unit cost Must show that a finished device can be made under $60,000 CAD. Additional Outcomes The proposed solution should: 1. Desirable range It is desirable to have a device that has greater standoff range in excess of 2m. The accuracy in ranging the MA would ideally be less than 1% relative error. Maximum sensing distance is desirable. The device should provide an azimuth to +/- 1 degree, and an inclination of +/- 1 degree. 2. Rough characterization The device provides a rough but human interpretable shape of the object, that allows the object to be characterized or even identified. 3. Sensitivity Produce a prototype capable of surpassing 10 fT sensitivity. 4. Specificity Ability to characterize and identify magnetic anomalies (objects with a known magnetic signature). 5. Quiet Device should be silent (vibration/audible signature). 6. Desired Configuration Device does not emit acoustic, electromagnetic (EM), and/or heat signature. Can run in both low and high humidity in temperature extremes from -20 to +40C, under conditions of vibration, and through cluttered barriers (e.g.; barrier material convoluted with wiring, and magnetic structural material) 7. Target Scale Desirable to be used against both large (room sized) and small (hardware or package sized) enclosures or objects. 8. Static vs oscillating field detection Ability to differentiate between static and oscillating magnetic fields. 9. Characterization of magnetic anomalies/sources Ability to characterize and identify magnetic anomalies. Ability to discern shape and size +/- 1 cm. 10. Human factor / accessibility considerations Device should be suitably adapted as to be easy to train on, easy to use (intuitive), and be in a shape or form
